newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico pact seen nudging up December inflation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico pact seen nudging up December inflation.

text.p: Inflationary pressures in Mexico will likely increase slightly at the end of the year due to the newly unveiled Alliance for Economic Growth plan, economists said on Monday.
An eight percent increase in gasoline prices and a 17 percent rise in the minimum wage due to take effect on December 1 will increase economists expectations for December inflation.
"It will have an effect on the December inflation figure ...especially the gas price hikes," said Gray Newman, James Capel's chief economist for Mexico.
Newman estimates the price hikes will add about 0.6 to 0.7 percentage points to the December CPI figure.
Enrique Quintana, a financial columnist for Mexico City's Reforma newspaper, said year-end inflation would likely top the government's 25 percent projection.
